headline: Fed study warns El Niño could drive US inflation in 2027
summary: A Federal Reserve of San Francisco study indicates that the El Niño climate phenomenon poses a significant risk of increased US inflation in 2027, though it may also support job growth.
why: Climate-driven weather patterns can disrupt agricultural supply chains and energy markets, leading to price volatility that central banks must account for when setting monetary policy.

impacts.name: United States
impacts.why: Inflationary pressures could influence future Federal Reserve interest rate decisions.
